topics.title: Binary Numbers
topics.concept: PLCs and computers store numbers in binary (base 2). Each bit position is a power of two, reading right to left: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 … A 1 means that place value is included; a 0 means it is not. To convert binary to decimal, add the place values of every position holding a 1.

resources.title: Learn how to read binary in 5 minutes

questions.prompt: What decimal number does the binary value 1010 represent?
What is the decimal number 13 in 4-bit binary?
questions.explanation: 13 = 8 + 4 + 1, so the bits for 8, 4, and 1 are set: 1101.

questions.prompt: In an 8-bit byte, what place value does the most significant (leftmost) bit represent?
questions.explanation: The leftmost bit of an 8-bit byte is 2⁷ = 128. The eight positions (right to left) are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128.

topics.title: Inductance
topics.concept: An inductor opposes changes in current by storing and releasing magnetic energy. In an AC circuit it produces a frequency-dependent opposition called inductive reactance (XL). In a pure inductor, current LAGS voltage by 90°. Because XL is proportional to frequency, at DC (0 Hz) an ideal inductor looks like a short circuit, and at very high frequency it looks like an open circuit.

diagram.caption: Inductive reactance
diagram.code:
XL = 2πƒL
XL = ωL    (ω = 2πƒ)

ƒ = frequency in hertz
L = inductance in henries
XL = reactance in ohms

XL ↑ as ƒ ↑

resources.title: AC Inductance and Inductive Reactance (Electronics Tutorials)

questions.prompt: What is the inductive reactance of a 0.5 H inductor at 60 Hz?
In a pure inductor, the current ___ the voltage by 90°.
questions.explanation: Current through a pure inductor LAGS the voltage by 90° (a mnemonic: ELI the ICE man — in an inductor (L), voltage (E) leads current (I)).

questions.prompt: A 2 H inductor is connected to a 50 Hz supply. What is its inductive reactance in ohms? (Round to the nearest whole number; enter a number.)
questions.explanation: XL = 2πƒL = 2 × π × 50 × 2 ≈ 628.3 Ω, which rounds to 628 Ω.

topics.title: Capacitance
topics.concept: A capacitor opposes changes in voltage. In an AC circuit it produces capacitive reactance (XC), which is inversely proportional to frequency. In a pure capacitor, current LEADS voltage by 90°. At DC (0 Hz) a capacitor looks like an open circuit, and at very high frequency it looks like a short circuit — the mirror image of an inductor.

diagram.caption: Capacitive reactance
diagram.code:
XC = 1 / (2πƒC)

ƒ = frequency in hertz
C = capacitance in farads
XC = reactance in ohms

XC ↓ as ƒ ↑   (high ƒ → short circuit)
XC ↑ as ƒ ↓   (DC → open circuit)

resources.title: AC Capacitance and Capacitive Reactance (Electronics Tutorials)

questions.prompt: As frequency increases, capacitive reactance (XC) ___.
questions.explanation: XC = 1/(2πƒC), so XC is inversely proportional to frequency: as ƒ rises, XC falls.

questions.prompt: In a pure capacitor, the current ___ the voltage by 90°.
questions.explanation: Current through a pure capacitor LEADS the voltage by 90° (the 'ICE' in 'ELI the ICE man').

questions.prompt: What is the capacitive reactance of a 10 µF capacitor at 50 Hz, in ohms? (Round to the nearest whole number; enter a number.)

topics.title: Motor Service Factor
topics.concept: Service factor (SF) is a multiplier on a motor's rated horsepower that indicates how much sustained overload the motor can tolerate under its nameplate conditions. It is defined by NEMA MG 1. Typical SF values are 1.0 or 1.15. A 10 HP motor with SF = 1.15 can run continuously up to about 11.5 HP under rated conditions. Relying on the service factor for continuous overload reduces the motor's insulation and life margin.

diagram.caption: Service factor (SF)
diagram.code:
SF = multiplier on rated horsepower

SF = 1.0  → 10 HP motor runs up to 10 HP
SF = 1.15 → 10 HP motor runs up to ~11.5 HP

(under nameplate rated conditions)
Continuous use of SF reduces life margin

resources.title: Motor Service Factor (SF) defined by NEMA

questions.prompt: A 10 HP motor has a service factor of 1.15. Under nameplate rated conditions, up to what sustained load can it run continuously?
questions.explanation: Continuous capacity ≈ rated HP × SF = 10 × 1.15 = 11.5 HP.

questions.prompt: What does a service factor greater than 1.0 indicate about a motor?
options: It can run above its rated HP for a time under rated conditions
It has a higher voltage rating
questions.explanation: SF > 1.0 means the motor has some overload margin above rated HP under the nameplate conditions.

questions.prompt: Continuously relying on the service factor for overload ___.
options: reduces insulation and motor life margin
questions.explanation: Running into the service factor means running hotter than rated, which reduces insulation and overall life margin.

topics.title: Fusing & Overcurrent Protection
topics.concept: Fuses protect conductors and equipment from overcurrent. A fuse has three key ratings: its continuous current rating (amps it carries), its voltage rating (the circuit voltage class), and its interrupting (AIC) rating (the maximum fault current it can safely clear). Time-delay (dual-element) fuses combine a short-circuit element with a thermal element, so they tolerate motor starting inrush while still opening on sustained overload. Fast-acting fuses open more quickly and suit sensitive loads without inrush.

diagram.caption: Fuse ratings to check
diagram.code:
• Current rating (A)  → continuous carry
• Voltage rating (V)  → circuit voltage class
• Interrupting rating (AIC / kA) → fault current it can safely clear

Time-delay (dual-element) → rides through motor inrush
Fast-acting → quicker open for sensitive loads

questions.prompt: Which fuse type is typically used on motor circuits to ride through starting inrush?
questions.explanation: Dual-element (time-delay) fuses combine a thermal element with a short-circuit element, so they tolerate motor inrush while still clearing sustained overloads.

questions.prompt: A fuse's interrupting (AIC) rating describes ___.
options: the maximum fault current it can safely clear
questions.explanation: The interrupting rating (amperes interrupting capacity, AIC) is the highest fault current the fuse can interrupt without damage.

questions.prompt: A fuse's continuous current rating describes ___.
options: the current it can carry continuously without opening
the fault current it can clear
questions.explanation: The current rating is the continuous current the fuse can carry; sustained current above this melts the element.

topics.title: Current Transformers (CTs)
topics.concept: A current transformer (CT) steps a large primary current down to a smaller, safer secondary current — typically 5 A or 1 A — for metering and protection relays. A CT has a single-turn (or few-turn) primary and a many-turn secondary. Safety-critical rule: never open-circuit an energized CT secondary. An open secondary can develop a dangerously high voltage and damage the CT and its insulation. The secondary must always be shorted or connected to a burden when the primary is energized.

diagram.caption: Current transformer basics
diagram.code:
Large primary current
      ↓ (CT steps it down)
Small secondary current — typically 5 A or 1 A
      ↓
Meter / protection relay

⚠ NEVER open-circuit an energized CT secondary

resources.title: Current Transformer Protection (Metrosil)

questions.prompt: What is a typical standard secondary current for a current transformer?
questions.explanation: Standard CT secondary currents are typically 5 A or 1 A, chosen to be safe for meters and relays.

questions.prompt: What must you NEVER do to an energized CT secondary?
options: Measure it with a clamp meter
questions.explanation: Opening an energized CT secondary can produce a dangerously high voltage. It must always be shorted or connected to a burden.

questions.prompt: The primary purpose of a CT is to ___ a large primary current for metering and protection.
questions.explanation: A CT steps a large current down to a smaller, standardized secondary current for instruments and relays.

topics.title: Step-up Transformer
topics.concept: A transformer transfers AC power between circuits by magnetic coupling. A step-up transformer has more turns on the secondary than the primary (Ns > Np), so it raises voltage and, in an ideal transformer, lowers current. The turns ratio sets the voltage ratio: Np/Ns = Vp/Vs. An ideal transformer conserves power, so Vp·Ip = Vs·Is — when voltage steps up, current steps down.

diagram.caption: Step-up transformer relationships
diagram.code:
Step-up →  Ns > Np

Turns ratio:  Np / Ns = Vp / Vs

Ideal power:  Vp·Ip = Vs·Is

Step-up →  Vs > Vp   and   Is < Ip

resources.title: Transformer Basics and Transformer Principles (Electronics Tutorials)

questions.prompt: A transformer has 100 primary turns and 1,000 secondary turns, with a 120 V primary. What is the secondary voltage?
In an ideal step-up transformer, which is true?
options: Voltage and current both stay the same
questions.explanation: An ideal transformer conserves power (Vp·Ip = Vs·Is), so a voltage step-up comes with a proportional current step-down.

questions.prompt: In a step-up transformer, how do the primary and secondary turns compare?
questions.explanation: A step-up transformer has more secondary turns than primary turns (Ns > Np), which raises the voltage.

topics.title: Three-phase Motor Connection
topics.concept: Three-phase motors connect their three windings in either wye (Y) or delta (Δ). The choice sets how much voltage each winding sees relative to the line voltage. In wye, each winding sees the phase voltage = line voltage ÷ √3 (line current = phase current). In delta, each winding sees the full line voltage (line current = √3 × phase current). On a 480 V system, a wye winding sees about 277 V, while a delta winding sees the full 480 V.

resources.title: Understanding the Basics of Delta Transformer Calculations (EC&M)

questions.prompt: In a wye-connected three-phase motor, each winding sees ___.
questions.explanation: In wye, each winding is connected line-to-neutral, so it sees the phase voltage = line voltage ÷ √3.

questions.prompt: In a delta-connected motor, each winding sees ___.
questions.explanation: In delta, each winding is connected directly across two lines, so it sees the full line voltage.

questions.prompt: In a delta connection, the line current equals ___.
questions.explanation: In delta, line current is √3 times the phase (winding) current: I_line = √3 × I_phase.

topics.title: Delta & Wye — Phase vs. Line
topics.concept: Balanced three-phase systems have two ways to relate line quantities to phase quantities. Wye (Y): line voltage is √3 × phase voltage, and line current equals phase current. Delta (Δ): line voltage equals phase voltage, and line current is √3 × phase current. Balanced three-phase real power is P = √3 × V_line × I_line × PF (and apparent power S = √3 × V_line × I_line).

resources.title: Understanding the Basics of Delta Transformer Calculations (EC&M)
Delta and Wye — phase and line relationships (video)

questions.prompt: In a balanced wye (Y) connection, the line voltage is ___ the phase voltage.
questions.explanation: In wye, V_line = √3 × V_phase.

questions.prompt: In a balanced delta (Δ) connection, the line current is ___ the phase current.
questions.explanation: In delta, I_line = √3 × I_phase.

questions.prompt: Balanced three-phase real power is calculated as ___.
questions.explanation: P = √3 × V_line × I_line × PF for a balanced three-phase load.

topics.title: Series & Parallel Circuits
topics.concept: In a series circuit, components share one path: the same current flows through each, total resistance is the sum (Rₜ = R₁ + R₂ + …), and voltage divides across them. In a parallel circuit, components share the same two nodes: voltage is equal across every branch, current divides, and total resistance follows 1/Rₜ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + … (two equal resistors in parallel give half of one).

resources.title: Understanding series and parallel circuits (free lecture chapter)

questions.prompt: Two 10 Ω resistors are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: Series resistances add: Rₜ = 10 Ω + 10 Ω = 20 Ω.

questions.prompt: Two 10 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
questions.explanation: 1/Rₜ = 1/10 + 1/10 = 2/10, so Rₜ = 10/2 = 5 Ω. Two equal resistors in parallel give half of one.

questions.prompt: In a series circuit, which quantity is the same through every component?
questions.explanation: A series circuit provides a single path, so the same current flows through every component. Voltage divides across them.

topics.title: AC Drives (VFDs)
topics.concept: A variable-frequency drive (VFD) controls AC motor speed by converting the fixed line AC to DC (rectifier), then back to variable-frequency, variable-voltage AC (inverter). Because a motor's synchronous speed is proportional to the applied frequency (n ≈ 120·f / poles), changing the VFD output frequency changes the motor speed. Lowering frequency lowers speed.

diagram.caption: VFD power flow and speed
diagram.code:
AC in → rectifier → DC bus → inverter → variable-freq AC out

Motor synchronous speed:
n ≈ 120·ƒ / poles

Lower ƒ → lower speed

resources.title: AC Drive Working Principle (ACDrive.org)
What is an AC Drive? (ABB / Empowering Pumps)

questions.prompt: What is the correct power-flow sequence through a VFD?
questions.explanation: A VFD rectifies line AC to DC, then inverts the DC back to variable-frequency AC for the motor.

questions.prompt: A 4-pole induction motor runs near its synchronous speed at 60 Hz. What is that synchronous speed?
To slow an AC motor with a VFD, you primarily ___.
questions.explanation: Motor speed is proportional to applied frequency, so reducing the VFD's output frequency reduces speed.

topics.title: Switches (SPST, SPDT, DPDT)
topics.concept: A switch's poles are the number of separate circuits it controls, and its throws are the number of output positions per pole. SPST (single pole, single throw) is a simple on/off. SPDT (single pole, double throw) routes a common terminal to one of two outputs. DPDT (double pole, double throw) controls two circuits, each with a common and two outputs. A grounding switch is used to safely connect a conductor or piece of equipment to ground for maintenance.

diagram.caption: Common switch types
rows: Common to one of two outputs
Two circuits, each common to two outputs

resources.title: Switch Types (All About Circuits)

questions.prompt: What does SPST stand for?
questions.explanation: SPST = Single Pole, Single Throw — a simple on/off switch.

questions.prompt: An SPDT switch routes a common terminal to ___.
questions.explanation: SPDT (single pole, double throw) has one common and two throws, so it selects one of two outputs.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a grounding switch?
options: Safely connect a conductor or equipment to ground for maintenance
questions.explanation: A grounding switch connects a conductor or equipment to ground so it can be worked on safely.

topics.title: PLC — Coils & Contacts
topics.concept: In ladder logic, a coil is an output instruction that is energized (true) when its rung logic is true. Contacts are input conditions read by the logic: a normally-open (NO) contact is true when its input is energized, and a normally-closed (NC) contact is true when its input is NOT energized. A seal-in (latch) circuit keeps a coil on after a momentary start releases by placing a contact driven by the output coil in parallel with the start contact.

resources.title: Ladder Logic Tutorial (PLC Academy)
PLC Handbook (AutomationDirect)

questions.prompt: In ladder logic, a coil represents an ___.
questions.explanation: A coil is an output instruction — it is energized when the rung's logic is true.

questions.prompt: A normally-closed (NC) contact is true when its input is ___.
questions.explanation: NC contacts pass logic when the input is NOT energized; energizing the input opens them.

questions.prompt: A seal-in (latch) circuit keeps the coil on after the momentary start releases by placing ___ in parallel with the start contact.
options: a contact driven by the output coil
questions.explanation: The seal-in contact (an aux contact of the output coil) closes when the coil energizes, holding the rung true after the start releases.

topics.title: Sinking & Sourcing
topics.concept: Sinking and sourcing describe the direction of DC current flow between a sensor/output and a PLC input. A sourcing (PNP) output sources (supplies) current out to the load. A sinking (NPN) output sinks (receives) current into the device. An input module is described from the opposite perspective: a 'sinking input' expects a sourcing device, and a 'sourcing input' expects a sinking device.

diagram.caption: Sourcing vs. sinking
rows: Sources current OUT to the load

resources.title: What is the Difference Between Sink and Source Logic? (Oriental Motor)

questions.prompt: A sourcing output ___ current to the load.
questions.explanation: A sourcing output pushes current out to the load; it is the source of the current.

questions.prompt: PNP devices are typically associated with which logic?
questions.explanation: PNP outputs are sourcing devices — they source current out to the load.

questions.prompt: A 'sinking input' on a controller expects to be driven by a ___ device.
questions.explanation: Input and output descriptions are opposites: a sinking input needs a sourcing (current-supplying) device to drive it.

topics.title: Impedance & Reactance
topics.concept: Reactance (X) is the AC opposition caused by inductance or capacitance. Impedance (Z) is the total opposition, combining resistance (R, the real part) and reactance (X, the imaginary part). For a series R-L circuit, Z = R + jXL; for a series R-C circuit, Z = R − jXC. The magnitude of the impedance is |Z| = √(R² + X²).

diagram.caption: Impedance relationships
diagram.code:
Z = R + jX

|Z| = √(R² + X²)

Series R–L:  Z = R + jXL
Series R–C:  Z = R − jXC

resources.title: AC Inductance and Inductive Reactance (Electronics Tutorials)
AC Capacitance and Capacitive Reactance (Electronics Tutorials)

questions.prompt: Impedance (Z) is the ___ of resistance and reactance.
questions.explanation: Z combines the real part R and the imaginary part jX, so its magnitude is the vector (Pythagorean) sum: |Z| = √(R² + X²).

questions.prompt: A series R-L circuit has R = 3 Ω and XL = 4 Ω. What is the magnitude of its impedance in ohms? (Enter a number.)
For a series R-C circuit, the impedance is Z = ___.
questions.explanation: Capacitive reactance contributes a negative imaginary part, so Z = R − jXC for a series R-C circuit.

topics.title: Dynamic Braking
topics.concept: Dynamic braking stops a motor by dissipating its kinetic (rotational) energy as heat in a braking resistor, rather than letting it coast. During braking, the motor temporarily acts as a generator, and the generated energy is dumped into a resistor (or applied as DC injection) to produce retarding torque.

diagram.caption: Dynamic braking energy path
diagram.code:
Rotating motor → acts as a generator
→ generated energy dumped into a braking resistor
→ energy dissipated as heat
→ retarding torque slows the motor

resources.title: What is Dynamic Braking? (Wolf Automation)

questions.prompt: Dynamic braking stops a motor by dissipating its kinetic energy as ___.
questions.explanation: The motor's rotational energy is dumped into a braking resistor and dissipated as heat.

questions.prompt: During dynamic braking, the motor temporarily acts as a ___.
questions.explanation: The spinning rotor generates voltage, so the motor acts briefly as a generator whose output is dissipated.

questions.prompt: The braking energy is typically dumped into ___.
questions.explanation: A braking resistor absorbs the generated energy, converting it to heat to provide retarding torque.

topics.title: Ohm's Law & Power
topics.concept: Ohm's Law relates voltage, current, and resistance: V = I × R (volts = amps × ohms). Rearranged, I = V ÷ R and R = V ÷ I. Electrical power is P = V × I; combined with Ohm's Law that gives P = I² × R and P = V² ÷ R. These relationships underpin conductor sizing, fusing, and load calculations.

diagram.caption: The core relationships
diagram.code:
V = I × R      (volts = amps × ohms)
I = V ÷ R      (amps = volts ÷ ohms)
R = V ÷ I      (ohms = volts ÷ amps)

P = V × I      (watts = volts × amps)
P = I² × R     (watts = amps² × ohms)
P = V² ÷ R     (watts = volts² ÷ ohms)

questions.prompt: A load with a resistance of 6 Ω is connected across a 24 V supply. How much current flows?
questions.explanation: Use I = V ÷ R = 24 V ÷ 6 Ω = 4 A. (The 144 A trap multiplies V × R instead of dividing.)

questions.prompt: A heater draws 10 A on a 120 V circuit. What is its power draw?
A 240 V supply drives 8 A through a load. What is the load's resistance in ohms? (Enter a number.)

topics.title: Induction Motors & Inrush Current
topics.concept: When an AC induction motor starts, it briefly draws a much higher current than its full-load current — this is inrush (also called locked-rotor or starting current). Inrush is commonly on the order of several times (often about 6×) full-load current, and it decays quickly as the motor spins up. Inrush matters for fuse and breaker sizing, which is one reason dual-element (time-delay) fuses are used on motor circuits.

diagram.caption: Inrush current
diagram.code:
Starting (inrush) current:
~ several × (often ~6×) full-load current

Decays quickly as the motor spins up to speed

Matters for fuse / breaker sizing

resources.title: What is inrush current in an AC motor? (Motion Control Tips)

questions.prompt: When an AC induction motor starts, it briefly draws ___ its full-load current.
questions.explanation: Starting (inrush) current is commonly several times full-load current, often around 6×, before decaying.

questions.prompt: As an induction motor spins up to speed, its inrush current ___.
questions.explanation: Inrush is highest at standstill (locked rotor) and decays as the motor accelerates toward operating speed.

questions.prompt: Why are dual-element (time-delay) fuses commonly used on motor circuits?
options: To ride through starting inrush without nuisance opening
questions.explanation: The thermal element tolerates the brief inrush, while the short-circuit element still clears sustained overloads and faults.

topics.title: Speed Control of a Shunt Motor
topics.concept: A DC shunt motor has its field winding connected in parallel (shunt) with the armature. Its speed can be controlled by varying the field current or the armature voltage. Weakening the field (reducing field current) raises the speed, while reducing the armature voltage lowers the speed. A shunt motor has relatively constant speed under changing load — good speed regulation.

diagram.caption: Shunt motor speed control
diagram.code:
Field winding ∥ armature (shunt connection)

Weaken field (↓ field current) → ↑ speed
Reduce armature voltage        → ↓ speed

Shunt motor → good speed regulation under load

resources.title: Speed Control of DC Shunt Motor (Your Electrical Guide)

questions.prompt: Weakening the field (reducing field current) of a shunt motor ___ its speed.
questions.explanation: Reducing field flux causes the armature to speed up to maintain back-EMF balance, so speed rises.

questions.prompt: Reducing the armature voltage of a shunt motor ___ its speed.
questions.explanation: Armature voltage control lowers the applied voltage, reducing speed.

questions.prompt: The field winding of a shunt motor is connected ___ the armature.
questions.explanation: 'Shunt' means the field winding is in parallel with the armature.

topics.title: Power Factor (VA = W / PF)
topics.concept: Power factor (PF) is the ratio of real power (watts) to apparent power (volt-amps). It measures how efficiently current is converted into useful work. For sinusoidal AC, PF = cos θ, where θ is the phase angle between voltage and current. Rearranged, VA = W / PF. A low power factor means more current is drawn for the same real power, which increases apparent-power demand.

diagram.caption: Power factor relationships
diagram.code:
PF = W / VA = cos θ

VA = W / PF

Low PF → more current for the same real power (W)

resources.title: Power Factor Formula (Fluke)

questions.prompt: Power factor is the ratio of ___ to ___.
questions.explanation: PF = W / VA — real power (watts) divided by apparent power (volt-amps).

questions.prompt: A load draws 1,200 W at a power factor of 0.8. What is its apparent power in VA? (Enter a number.)
A low power factor means ___ for the same real power.
questions.explanation: At a given real power, a lower PF requires more apparent power (VA) and therefore more current.

topics.title: Logic Gates
topics.concept: Logic gates are the building blocks of digital circuits. AND outputs 1 only when all inputs are 1. OR outputs 1 when at least one input is 1. NOT inverts its single input. XOR (exclusive-OR) outputs 1 when its inputs differ. NAND, NOR, and XNOR are the inverses of AND, OR, and XOR respectively (NAND = NOT-AND, NOR = NOT-OR, XNOR = NOT-XOR).

resources.title: Logic gates: AND, OR, XOR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XNOR (TechTarget)

questions.prompt: A two-input AND gate outputs 1 when ___.
questions.explanation: AND outputs 1 only when every input is 1 (0·1 = 0, 1·1 = 1).

questions.prompt: A two-input XOR gate outputs 1 when ___.
questions.explanation: XOR (exclusive-OR) is true only when exactly one input is 1 — i.e., the inputs differ.

questions.prompt: NAND is ___.
questions.explanation: NAND = NOT-AND: it outputs the inverse of an AND gate.

topics.title: Analog Input Resolution & Scaling
topics.concept: An analog input card converts a continuous signal (such as 4–20 mA or 0–10 V) into a digital count. The bit depth sets how finely it can resolve the signal: an n-bit converter gives 2ⁿ counts (12-bit = 4,096 counts, 16-bit = 65,536 counts). Resolution per count is approximately the full-scale span divided by 2ⁿ. To scale raw counts to engineering units, use EU = (raw − raw_min)/(raw_max − raw_min) × (EU_max − EU_min) + EU_min.

diagram.caption: Resolution and scaling
diagram.code:
n-bit converter → 2ⁿ counts
  12-bit = 4096 counts
  16-bit = 65536 counts

Resolution ≈ full-scale span / 2ⁿ

EU = (raw − raw_min)/(raw_max − raw_min)
       × (EU_max − EU_min) + EU_min

resources.title: Analog Input Card Resolution & Effects on Accuracy (Instrumentation Tools)

questions.prompt: A 12-bit analog-to-digital converter gives how many counts?
questions.explanation: 2¹² = 4,096 counts.

questions.prompt: How many counts does a 16-bit analog-to-digital converter provide? (Enter a number.)
questions.explanation: 2¹⁶ = 65,536 counts.

questions.prompt: What is the resolution per count of a 0–10 V signal read by a 12-bit input (4,096 counts)?
questions.explanation: Resolution ≈ 10 V / 4,096 ≈ 0.00244 V ≈ 2.44 mV per count.

topics.title: PLC Data Types
topics.concept: PLC programming uses typed data, and different types have different bit widths and ranges. BOOL is a single bit (true/false). INT is a 16-bit signed integer (−32,768 to 32,767). DINT is a 32-bit signed integer. REAL is a 32-bit floating-point number. Unsigned variants (UINT, UDINT) store only non-negative values across the same bit widths, and bytes/words/dwords group bits into 8/16/32-bit units.

resources.title: Data Types in PLC (Instrumentation Tools)

questions.prompt: What is the value range of a 16-bit signed INT?
questions.explanation: A 16-bit signed integer ranges from −2¹⁵ to 2¹⁵ − 1, i.e., −32,768 to 32,767.

questions.prompt: Which data type stores true/false values in a single bit?
questions.explanation: BOOL is a single-bit value: true (1) or false (0).

questions.prompt: REAL is a ___ data type.
questions.explanation: REAL is a 32-bit IEEE floating-point type, used for values with fractional parts.

topics.title: Ladder Logic — Start/Stop & Seal-in
topics.concept: This is an original motor start/stop rung. The momentary Start (NO) button energizes the Run coil. A seal-in contact driven by the Run coil is wired in parallel with Start, so the coil stays energized after Start releases. The Stop (NC) button and the overload (NC) contact sit in series with the coil: opening either one de-energizes the motor. Pressing Stop (or an overload trip) breaks the rung and drops the Run coil.

diagram.caption: Start/stop rung with seal-in and overload

resources.title: Ladder Logic Tutorial (PLC Academy)

questions.prompt: What keeps the Run coil energized after the momentary Start button is released?
options: The seal-in contact (an aux contact of the Run coil) in parallel with Start
questions.explanation: The seal-in contact closes when the Run coil energizes, holding the rung true after Start releases.

questions.prompt: Where is the overload (OL) contact typically placed in a motor start/stop rung?
options: In series with the Run coil
questions.explanation: The OL NC contact is in series with the coil, so an overload trip opens it and drops the motor out.

questions.prompt: What happens when the NC Stop button is pressed?
options: It opens and de-energizes the Run coil
It closes and energizes the Run coil
questions.explanation: The Stop button is normally-closed; pressing it opens the rung, removing power from the Run coil.

topics.title: Review — Mixed Practice
topics.concept: Original mixed review covering the core skills from the other topics: transformer turns and voltage ratios, wye/delta phase-to-line relationships, three-phase power, and motor overcurrent protection.

diagram.caption: Quick reference
diagram.code:
Turns ratio:  Np / Ns = Vp / Vs
Wye:  V_line = √3 × V_phase
Delta: I_line = √3 × I_phase
Three-phase power:  P = √3 × V_line × I_line × PF

questions.prompt: A transformer has 200 primary turns and 50 secondary turns, with a 480 V primary. What is the secondary voltage?
A 208 V three-phase supply is applied to a wye-connected motor. What is the phase voltage across each winding?
questions.explanation: In wye, each winding sees V_phase = V_line ÷ √3 = 208 ÷ 1.732 ≈ 120 V.

questions.prompt: A balanced three-phase load draws 10 A per line at 480 V line with a power factor of 0.9. Its real power is about ___.
Which fuse type best suits a motor circuit that must ride through starting inrush?
questions.explanation: Dual-element (time-delay) fuses tolerate starting inrush while still clearing sustained overloads and faults.
